correctness.rationale: The one final claim is an exact finite table for each n=1,...,6. The published unique-canonical-word theorem characterizes representatives by the between-repetitions requirement. The standalone pure-Python exhaustive prefix enumerator generates precisely all valid canonical strings; a second independent generator closure using defining reductions gives identical full word sets in all six cases. Level counts are computed by the published greedy right multiplication rule and independently by deletion and normalization; they agree elementwise for 85823 words. Replayed code gives the complete table in RESULT.md, and orders match OEIS A125625. No finite sample is extrapolated to all n; the finite symmetry was asserted only for the six exhaustive cases.

value.rationale: The original April 2026 paper introduces a natural semigroup ultrametric but computes only extreme spheres. This exact radius-by-radius census supplies the first interior data through six generators for a canonical, previously unexplored metric invariant. It is a complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary unmotivated slice: n=6 already comprises 83973 distinct words while n=7 has 22263378. The interior counts 13170 and 27106 cannot be read off from total orders or extreme formulas, and the finite palindromicity pattern yields meaningful reproducible evidence for future semigroup and ultrametric investigations. No general law or unproved extension is claimed, and novelty of the old total counts is explicitly disavowed.
